tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air — Pressure Matters
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is designed for airbrushing but may still require thinning for fine detail work. Mix at a 2:1 ratio with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for a workable consistency. Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint for smoother application. Spray at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure for consistent coverage. Test on a white plastic spoon — if it sprays evenly, you're good to go.

tips.title: Base Coat with Vallejo Model Color — Two Coats Better
tips.text: Vallejo Model Color is ideal for base coats due to its pigment density. Apply the first coat diluted at a 1:1 ratio with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner at 1.0 bar pressure. Allow 24 hours drying time. Apply the second coat undiluted at 1.5 bar pressure for better adhesion and coverage. Sand lightly with fine sandpaper after drying to remove any orange peel.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking — Tamiya Tape and Mr. Hobby Markers
tips.text: For camouflage patterns, use Tamiya Tape to mask off sections. Apply gently to avoid lifting paint later. Use Mr. Hobby Markers to draw stripes or panel lines before painting to create hard edges. Paint each section with Vallejo Model Air or Color, allowing each coat to dry completely before removing tape. Start with smaller sections to avoid lifting paint.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes — Dilute for Control
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes provide great contrast but can be too dark if not diluted. Dilute with AK Interactive Thinner at a 3:1 ratio (3 parts thinner, 1 part wash) for better control. Apply with a fine brush or by dabbing onto raised areas. Work quickly and wipe away excess with a damp Q-tip before it dries. Allow 24 hours drying time before removing excess with a soft brush.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponge Technique — Alclad II and Mr. Hobby
tips.text: Create realistic chipping using a makeup sponge and Alclad II Clear Primer. Paint the area to be chipped with Vallejo Model Color. Once dry, dab the sponge lightly in Alclad II Clear Primer and pat gently onto the painted surface. Use varying pressure for different chip sizes. Allow drying, then gently wipe away excess primer with a damp Q-tip. Apply final washes and weathering.
